newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria starts work on gas pipe for industry.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria starts work on gas pipe for industry.

text.p: Nigeria's state run gas company on Friday said it had begun laying an $18 million pipeline to supply industries in Lagos with natural gas that is currently being flared.

"We have commenced laying of the pipes following the release of funds by the government," Jackson Gaius-Obaseki, managing director of the Nigerian Gas Company, a subsidiary of state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation told Reuters.
"It should be concluded by end of first quarter in 1997."
The project, being handled by Saipem Nigeria, will lay a spur to the pipeline which already links the Egbin power station in Lagos with the Escravos oil field.
The gas company has already entered into long term gas supply contracts with four firms -- Guinness, Cadbury, Paterson Zochonis and Kew Metal Works.
Nigeria has proven gas reserves of 110 trillion cubic feet.
However most of what is produced as a consequence of crude oil extraction is currently flared.
"The aim now is to ensure that many industries use natural gas as source of energy," Gaius-Obaseki said.
